Understanding of basic knowledge of integral calculus of single-variable functions.
Handling of differential calculus techniques for locating extrema, local approximation of functions, and numerical resolution of systems of equations.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to real numbers. Absolute value. The Euclidean space R^n. Sequences. Series. Limits and continuity of single and multivariable functions. Bolzano's Theorem. Weierstrass's Theorem.

Differential calculus of single real variable functions: mean value theorem, L'Hôpital's rule, Taylor's theorem, study of extrema, convexity. Differential calculus of multivariable real functions: partial derivatives, directional derivatives, differentiability, Jacobian matrix, chain rule, Hessian matrix, relative extrema.
The Riemann integral. Fundamental theorem of calculus. Barrow's rule. Change of variable. Calculation of antiderivatives. Improper integrals. Applications of the integral.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving: The professor will solve typical problems and exercises, and the student will have to solve similar exercises.
Laboratory practices: Computational tools will be used to solve exercises and apply the knowledge obtained in theory classes.
Lectures: The professor will present the subject's content in theoretical classes.

assessment_methods.method: Problem-solving and/or exercises (written controls and/or assignments)

assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is based on problem-solving/exercises (60%) and a final exam (40%). Students not opting for continuous assessment will take a final exam covering all course content, accounting for 100% of the grade. The second call assessment will also be a final exam covering all course content, accounting for 100% of the grade. Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized use of electronic devices, etc.) will result in a failing grade (0.0).
